title: Recipe 15 — Skills (a registry of procedures the model opts into)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “A skill is a markdown procedure the model chooses to load. Frontmatter costs tokens at boot; the body costs nothing until it's called.”

beats.label: Blank the scratch spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beat — watching the model pick a skill means really calling it.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the harness skills attach to

beats.label: Type recipe 01's harness
beats.cue: “Skills are data, not spec surface — so start from the plainest recipe-01 agent, and change nothing about it.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean before a single skill exists — so anything that changes downstream is the skills' doing.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's release-checklist skill
beats.cue: “One directory, one SKILL.md: frontmatter with a name and a description, then a numbered procedure with an explicit stop point.”

beats.label: Open what we just wrote
beats.cue: “Second-person imperatives, tools named the way the model sees them, and a line that says where to stop. That's the whole authoring guidance.”

beats.label: Add the bug-triage skill
beats.cue: “Second procedure — and note it references linear__get_issue by its model-facing MCP name, not prose.”

beats.label: Add the code-review skill
beats.cue: “Third. Now we have a registry — and the point of the recipe is that three cost the same at boot as one, plus sixty tokens.”

beats.label: List the project layer
beats.cue: “Skills are file-discovered, so the directory listing IS the registry.” That's the recipe's first debugging move.

verify.note: bug-triage, code-review, release-checklist — the project layer, which overrides ~/.crewhaus/skills

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Nothing about skills appears in the IR. They're runtime data read from the working directory — which is exactly why no spec change was needed.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli — no skills field in it

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it from this directory — so the boot that runs is the one that discovers our three skills. GREEN, no key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Find the skill wiring in the emitted agent
beats.cue: “Three lines of generated code: wireMemory discovers them from cwd, createSkillTool registers the synthetic Skill tool. Nothing hidden.”

groups.title: Beat 4 · what the model sees at boot

beats.label: Run the real discovery, keylessly
beats.cue: “discoverSkills plus formatSkillsForPrompt — the actual runtime functions the bundle calls, from the bundle we just checked. This is the system-prompt block, not a mock-up.”
beats.command: bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { discoverSkills, formatSkillsForPrompt } from "@crewhaus/skills-registry"; const s = await discoverSkills({ cwd: "../..", homeDir: "/nonexistent" }); console.log(formatSkillsForPrompt(s))' > live/skills-at-boot.txt

verify.note: keyless — discovery is frontmatter parsing on disk. homeDir is pinned off the operator's real ~/.crewhaus/skills so the take is deterministic; redirect, not a pipe, so the exit code is bun's

beats.label: Read the rendered block
beats.cue: “One line per skill — name and description only. The bodies stayed on disk, which is the whole reason fifty skills isn't fifty system prompts.”

groups.title: One more thing · watch the model opt in

beats.label: Launch the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Same spec as recipe 01. The only difference is three files it found on the way up.”

beats.label: Say the word the skill was written for
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The model calls Skill({ name: "release-checklist" }) — and only then does the body cost anything.”

verify.note: lazy load: loadSkillBody reads the body from disk at call time and returns it as the tool output

beats.label: Open the recipe's boundary section
beats.cue: “A skill is model-discovered. If you need it on every call regardless of what the model wants, that's a hook — recipe 14.”
